_about: Linthra's reviewed inventory of fixed network destinations (#504).
scripts/check_network_destinations.py reads the source Linthra ships
(lib/, the Android app module, the Linux runner and packaging metadata,
native/ and the vendored packages in third_party/) and fails when a host
name or IP literal turns up that this file does not list, or turns up in a
file its entry does not cover.
Addresses the user types in (their Jellyfin, Navidrome/Subsonic, Plex or
Audiobookshelf server) are data, not code, and never belong here.
Each entry says what Linthra does with the host (kind), when it is
contacted if it is contacted at all (trigger, app-request only), which
builds carry it, which files may mention it and why. An entry whose paths
stop matching fails the check too, so a reason cannot outlive what it
Entries are sorted by (host, kind) and paths are sorted within an entry.
The checker enforces both. docs/network-destinations.md explains how to
review a new host and what this check does not prove.

kinds.app-request: Linthra's own code connects to this host
kinds.browser-link: Handed to the browser or mail client when the user taps a link; Linthra never fetches it
kinds.reference: Only mentioned in comments, hint text, licence headers, XML namespaces or packaging metadata; never contacted

destinations.rationale: Example LAN address in the Plex server field's hint text and validation message.
Example LAN server address in the comments that explain why cleartext HTTP is allowed.
